utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-81-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the appearances for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Representing the Office of the Prosecutor, I am Dermot Groome, accompanied by Karim Kahn Agha and Chester Stamp, and assisted by Skye Winner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. And for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAHN
utterances.text: Your Honour, you will have to make do, I'm afraid, with a simple Karim Kahn for the accused as duty counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm happy to have you, Mr. Kahn. Well, this, as you know, is the initial appearance of Mr. Momcilo Perisic. The hearing will be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Rule 62, and at the hearing the accused will be asked to enter a plea on the indictment in the case against him. Please stand, Mr. Perisic. Let me first ascertain whether you can hear the proceedings in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kahn, I take it that Mr. Perisic has received a copy of the indictment and that you have had the opportunity of going through the indictment with him and informing him of the nature of the charges against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAHN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have. He's read the indictment and he understands the nature of the charges that he faces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And as you're aware, the accused has the right to have the indictment read out in court before he pleads to it. He may also waive the right. What does he wish to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAHN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the accused is mindful of the preciousness of Court time and he's happy to waive his right as far as having the full indictment read out to him today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful for the cooperation. Mr. Perisic, you have heard what your counsel has said. You have the indictment in a language you understand. He has been through it with you, informed you of the nature of the charges against you. Now, you may enter a plea today or within 30 days of this appearance. Do you wish to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The counts in the indictment will be read out to you by the Court deputy. She will read the counts, and I will take your plea. Please commence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead, Mr. Perisic; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead, Mr. Perisic; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 3, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 4, attacks on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 51(2) of the Additional Protocol I and Article 13(2) of Additional Protocol II to the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 5.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5, murder, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 6.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 7.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 8.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Attacks on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 51(2) of Additional Protocol I and Article 13(2) of Additional Protocol II to the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 9.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 9, murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 10.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 10, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) and 7(3), of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 11.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(i) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 12.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 12, persecutions on political, racial or religious grounds, a crime against humanity, including murder, cruel and inhumane treatment and forcible transfer, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 13.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 13, extermination, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(b) and 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit. It only remains for me, Mr. Groome, to remind you of your obligation under Rule 66 to make available to the Defence within 30 days copies of the supporting material which accompany the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I recognise our obligations in that regard, and our intention is to fully comply with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kahn?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAHN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no matter that need trouble you to any great extent, but as a matter of information, the accused does have a lawyer of his own, Mr. Batic Vladan. It's hoped by the accused that OLAD would deal with his application to be admitted onto the Rule 45 list with its customary expedition. Your Honour that's particularly important in this case because the accused voluntarily surrendered to the jurisdiction of the Tribunal and it's very much in his interests, given his age, that a provisional release application is submitted by the lawyer of his own choice within the parameters of the Registrar's obligations at the earliest opportunity. Your Honour, that's just for your information at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I expect the Registrar will discharge his duties. There being no other matter, the hearing is adjourned.
